cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's just poured out his heart over his own people, Israel (Romans 9:2-4). Now he asks, "What then will we say?"
His answer starts with the Gentiles, who weren't pursuing righteousness at all. No jogging, no stretching, didn't even BUY the shoes.

cards.question: The Gentiles, who didn't pursue righteousness, have obtained it anyway.
What kind of righteousness did the Gentiles obtain?

cards.text: Then there's Israel, and Israel WAS chasing. They pursued a law of righteousness.

cards.question: Israel pursued a law of righteousness and attained it.

cards.text: So Paul asks the question we're all thinking: "Why not?"

cards.question: Why didn't Israel attain the righteousness they were chasing?

answers.text: They pursued it as if by works
They pursued it without the law

cards.text: They stumbled over the stumbling stone. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer tripping over the same dead battery every night, so I GET it.
Paul backs it up with Scripture. God says He lays a stone in Zion that people stumble over, a rock of offense.

cards.question: God lays a stumbling stone in Zion. What about the one who believes in Him?

answers.text: They will never be put to shame

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal. He calls his readers brothers and opens up about his own people.

cards.question: Paul says his heart's desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their ___.

cards.text: And Paul vouches for them: they're zealous for God. All in, full speed, no brakes.

cards.question: Paul says Israel's zeal for God is based on knowledge.

cards.text: They were ignorant of God's righteousness and tried to set up their own. That's flooring it with the GPS off: ALL the passion, wrong city.

cards.question: Israel tried to set up their own righteousness. What does Paul say they did not do with God's righteousness?
Paul writes that Christ is the ___ of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who ___.

cards.text: Now Paul puts two kinds of righteousness side by side. For the kind that's by the law, Moses, Israel's leader, writes: "The man who does these things will live by them."

cards.question: The righteousness by faith says not to ask in your heart who will ascend into heaven. Paul says that would be to do what?

cards.text: Same goes the other way: don't ask who will descend into the Abyss to bring Christ up from the dead. No ladder up, no shovel down, and friend, I can't even reach the TOP SHELF.

cards.question: The righteousness by faith says not to ask who will go up to heaven or down to the Abyss. Where does it say the word is?

answers.text: In your mouth and in your heart
On tablets of stone in Zion

cards.text: Paul says that's the word of faith they're proclaiming. And he lays it out, plain and simple.

cards.question: Paul says if you confess with your ___ that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your ___ that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

cards.text: With your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved. Then that line again: "Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame."

cards.question: Paul says that when it comes to being saved, there's a difference between Jew and Greek.
The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives ___ to all who call on Him.

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture: "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." EVERYONE, friend. No guest list, no bouncer, no "sorry, we're at capacity."

cards.question: Paul works backward: how can they call on the One they haven't believed, or believe in the One they haven't heard? And how can they hear without what?
Next in Paul's chain: how can they preach unless they are ___?

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!" Friend, NOBODY talks about feet like that unless the news is THAT good.

cards.question: Paul says all of them welcomed the good news.

cards.text: Isaiah, a prophet of Israel (Isaiah 1:1), even asks, "Lord, who has believed our message?" I bet that one stung.

cards.question: So Paul sums it up: faith comes by ___, and hearing by the word of Christ.

cards.text: Paul asks if they didn't hear, and says indeed they did: "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world." That's the whole PLANET on reply-all.
Then Paul asks, did Israel not understand? Moses says God will make them jealous by those who are not a nation, and angry by a nation without understanding.

cards.question: Isaiah boldly says God was found by people who did not seek Him.
As for Israel, what does God say He has been doing all day long?

answers.text: Holding out His hands to them
Turning His face away from them

findings.problem: Romans 10:4 is never set up on a story card. The choice card follows card 17, which covers 10:3, and asks the baker to supply the exact word 'end' in 'Christ is the ___ of the law'. Nothing earlier lets a baker reason to 'end' over 'keeper', so this is a guess at unseen wording rather than an informed pick.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen. The blank 'end' can't be worked out from meaning already given.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke stacks three images (a ladder up, a shovel down and the top shelf) and blends them with the Bible setting. 'Shovel down' sits right on 'bring Christ up from the dead', which also puts a digging gag next to Christ's resurrection.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card says 'the word of faith they're proclaiming'. The BSB says 'the word of faith we are proclaiming' (Romans 10:8). Paul is including himself, so 'they're' misstates who is proclaiming it.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Paul says all of them welcomed the good news' never says who 'them' is. The baker can't see the earlier card, so the statement has no clear subject.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Isaiah, a prophet of Israel (Isaiah 1:1)': Isaiah 1:1 doesn't call Isaiah a prophet. It calls his book a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem. The cited reference doesn't support the fact. A reference such as Isaiah 37:2 ('Isaiah the prophet') would, and 'of Israel' should match what that text says.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The passage ends on this choice card, and nothing ever tells the baker that God calls Israel 'a disobedient and obstinate people' (Romans 10:21). That is the closing detail of the passage, and it gets left out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'Faith comes by ___, and hearing by the word of Christ' gives away the blank 'hearing' in the same sentence. The question shows the answer, so the card tests almost nothing.
findings.question: Can a fill in the blank leave the right answer visible elsewhere in its own question? Or should a card like this blank a different word, or switch to another question type?
